dlg.harlan.first.0.note: Delighted, laughing at Jory's retelling. Narrator: he takes your hand. Then a little embarrassed formality: 'Any other day I'd have said that first.'

dlg.harlan.first.1.note: Narrator: the shutters, he doesn't get up. His name said without the patter. 'Everyone's heard.' A pause. 'Buy something, or don't.' empty.

dlg.harlan.first.2.note: Breaks off on 'That's—'. Narrator for the rush round the counter. Then questions tumbling, rising, the last one cracking: the boy.

dlg.harlan.first.3.note: Salesman's opener by habit, then he smells the Verge and the patter drops. 'Tell me you've seen something.' pleading.

dlg.harlan.first.4.note: Warm Bristol patter on the goods. Slower on Jory. 'He's never been a week late in his life.' breaks. Pause. 'Forgive me. I say that to everyone.' embarrassed.

dlg.harlan.first.5.note: As first.4: patter, then the crack on 'He's never six days late.'

dlg.harlan.first.6.note: As first.4: patter, then the crack on 'He's never five days late.'

dlg.harlan.first.7.intent: asks if you saw the wagons
dlg.harlan.first.7.note: Patter; a spark of hope on 'You came up the south road?', answered by himself: 'No. No, of course you didn't.' 'Four days.' a crack.

dlg.harlan.hub.1.note: 'I heard. I heard.' Pause. A small fond detail that hurts most: sulking if supper was late. Then hollow kindness.

dlg.harlan.hub.2.note: Narrator: he doesn't get up. Tired self-justification. 'Any word? No. There never is.' answers himself.

dlg.harlan.hub.3.note: Narrator: eyes on the bend. A fond imagined picture. 'Any word?' quiet.

dlg.harlan.what.0.note: Bitter about the wolves. Businesslike rewards; then the patter drops: 'The boy, I'll pay what you ask.' raw.

dlg.harlan.route.0.note: Facts he has repeated too often. 'Nobody saw them.' deflated.

dlg.harlan.jory.0.note: 'Alive. Alive!' the second almost a sob. Fumbling coins. Overflowing generosity. 'Don't tell anyone.' laughing.

dlg.harlan.box.0.note: Honest wonder at honesty. Thanks doubled.

dlg.harlan.pell.0.note: 'Pell. Pell!' disbelief then fury. Bitter on 'as a friend'. Hot determination at the end.

dlg.harlan.be.0.wants: to say as little as possible
dlg.harlan.be.0.note: A long hesitation. 'Six crates.' Justifying himself. 'B.E. Blasting ember.' said like spelling a guilt. Last sentence a weak joke.
dlg.harlan.be.0.say: ...Six crates. For a buyer I won't name. Paid in advance, in gold, which is why I asked no questions. B. E. Blasting ember. Somebody out there wants to dig a very big hole.

dlg.harlan.g.0.note: Too-quick salesman's joke. Changes the subject a beat too fast: 'Is there anything else?'

dlg.harlan.knew.0.note: Fond scorn for Jory. Repeats 'He didn't know.' quieter. Then the confession, barely said: 'I did.'

dlg.harlan.betrayed.0.intent: pays you anyway, and sends you off
dlg.harlan.betrayed.0.note: First sentence warm with memory; the second cold. Narrator: the coins counted. 'For the boy. I said I would.' dignity. Cold dismissal.

dlg.harlan.ash.0.note: Asks, dreading. Stops himself. 'Don't come to the funeral. There's nothing to bury.' breaking.

dlg.harlan.cb_exposed_pell.0.note: Bitter memory of the wine. Pause. 'Thank you. I think. I'll know when I've stopped feeling sick.' the family line, honest and queasy.

dlg.harlan.cb_sold_dig.0.note: A long beat. 'Well.' Then a rueful confession dressed as agreement.

dlg.harlan.cb_killed_greymuzzle.0.note: Fair-minded, then hard: 'I'll not pretend to weep.'

dlg.harlan.say_calling.0.note: Salesman's warmth; catches on 'if Jory—' and corrects himself.

dlg.harlan.say_calling.2.note: Salesman's banter; a bitter edge on 'Then what's it for?'

dlg.harlan.jory_now.0.note: Narrator: he looks at his hands. 'First time in his life.' A pause. 'He always did.' broken past tense.

dlg.harlan.jory_now.1.note: Fond list. Then guilt: 'He believed me; he always does.' The last line self-hatred, quiet.

dlg.harlan.t_harlan.0.note: Sad on his sister. A laugh in the voice for 'Do you have a horse?'. 'He named all of them wrong.' fond, wet-eyed.

dlg.harlan.roost.0.note: Narrator: he sits. 'Three. In cages.' numb. Narrator: counting, stops. The description of Jory loving and frightened; narrator: he stops. Then fierce: 'Get him out.'

dlg.harlan.ledger_early.0.note: Narrator: his finger stops. 'That's the night.' twice, the second hollow. Reading. Narrator: he looks up. Questions. Then pleading; the last line a frightening honesty.

dlg.harlan.crates.0.note: Narrator for his face. '...Are they.' Narrator: reaching for paper. Thanks a beat too quick. 'Paid for is paid for.' businesslike cover.

dlg.harlan.be_dig.0.note: Narrator: a long time. A salesman's creed, recited. Then the subject changes a beat too fast.

dlg.harlan.cb_jory_knows.0.note: Narrator: no good morning. 'He knows. You told him.' flat. Then a weak excuse, ashamed.
